_comment: Calibration constants. Every number here is either taken from a published estimate (cited) or is an explicit modelling assumption (marked assumption: true). Nothing is tuned to make the demo look good; the backtest is what checks them.

base_rates.citation: Phase-transition probabilities from 2025 analyses of >20,000 clinical development programmes; overall Phase I -> approval stabilised near 5-10%. Phase II is the dominant hurdle at ~28%.
base_rates.notes: The engine's prior is p_approval_from_phase1: the question it answers is 'if this mechanism entered the clinic, would it get through', not 'will this molecule work'.

failure_attribution.citation: Lack of clinical efficacy 40-50%, unmanageable toxicity ~30%, poor drug-like properties 10-15%, commercial/strategic ~10%.
failure_attribution.design_consequence: Three quarters of failure is biology (efficacy + on-target toxicity), not chemistry. So the engine scores the mechanism hypothesis, not the molecule.

lr_cap.rationale: Total likelihood ratio is capped so that no accumulation of correlated evidence can push a mechanism past ~74% posterior from a 10% prior. Even mechanisms with textbook-perfect human genetics (PCSK9) fail for reasons outside the evidence model: formulation, competitive landscape, trial execution. An uncapped multiplicative model is the classic way these systems become confidently wrong.

within_group_damping.rationale: Evidence classes inside one independence group are correlated (a GWAS hit and a coding-variant burden test read the same human genetic signal). The strongest class in a group counts in full; the rest are damped to 35%. Naive summation over correlated evidence is the single largest source of overconfidence in existing target-scoring tools.

harmonic_normaliser.citation: Open Targets normalises its harmonic sum by the maximum theoretical harmonic sum (~1.644, the limit of sum 1/i^2). Reused here so within-class aggregation behaves the same way researchers already expect from the Platform.

human_genetics_causal.label: Human genetics, causal-grade
human_genetics_causal.description: Coding or Mendelian variant with clear gene assignment and a known direction of effect in humans.
human_genetics_causal.citation: Minikel et al. 2024 (Nature) refined Nelson et al. 2015: mechanisms with genetic support are ~2.6x more likely to be approved; support from severe Mendelian disorders and protein-altering variants is the strongest subclass.

acquisition.name: Targeted human genetic association (biobank / burden test)
acquisition.description: Rare-variant burden and coding-variant association against the indication phenotype in an existing biobank. Cheap because the cohorts already exist; the cost is analyst time and access.

human_genetics_gwas.label: Human genetics, common variant
human_genetics_gwas.description: GWAS association at the locus without confident causal-gene assignment.
human_genetics_gwas.citation: Genetic support is materially weaker where the causal gene is ambiguous; non-coding association alone does not carry the full ~2x effect.

acquisition.name: GWAS locus-to-gene fine-mapping
acquisition.description: Statistical fine-mapping plus colocalisation with eQTL/pQTL to assign the causal gene at an associated locus.

human_perturbation.label: Human perturbation (drug, MR, or natural experiment)
human_perturbation.description: The target has actually been modulated in humans -- an approved or investigational drug, or Mendelian randomisation using a variant that proxies modulation -- and the phenotype moved.
human_perturbation.citation: Mendelian randomisation proxies the effect of perturbing a drug target and is used both for efficacy prediction and for anticipating on-target adverse events (e.g. IL-6 signalling inhibition predicts infection and dermatitis risk).

acquisition.name: Mendelian randomisation with a cis-pQTL instrument
acquisition.description: Use a cis-acting variant that changes target level/activity as an instrument for lifelong modulation, tested against the indication and against the full phenome for safety.

perturbation_biology.label: Perturbation in a human disease-relevant system
perturbation_biology.description: CRISPR knockout/knockdown or a tool compound in human primary cells or organoids modelling the tissue where the pathology lives.
perturbation_biology.citation: Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens in disease-relevant human models are integrated as a distinct evidence type by Open Targets (e.g. Project Score across 300 cancer models).

acquisition.name: CRISPR perturbation in patient-derived cells
acquisition.description: Knockout/knockdown plus rescue in the human cell type carrying the pathology, read out on a disease-proximal phenotype rather than a marker.

model_organism.label: Model organism phenotype
model_organism.description: Knockout or transgenic phenotype in mouse or another model organism.
model_organism.citation: Animal-model evidence is a standard Open Targets datatype but has the weakest translational record of the experimental classes; poor predictive models in discovery and preclinical research are a named driver of attrition.

acquisition.name: Mouse knockout / conditional model
acquisition.description: Expensive, slow, and the low specificity is the point: many targets give a mouse phenotype and no human effect.

expression_correlative.label: Expression / abundance correlation
expression_correlative.description: The target is differentially expressed or abundant in patient tissue.
expression_correlative.citation: Differential expression is an Open Targets datatype but is correlative: disease changes expression at least as often as expression changes disease.

acquisition.name: Single-cell / bulk differential expression in patient tissue
acquisition.description: High sensitivity, very low specificity. Useful for localisation and for choosing the cell type to perturb -- almost useless as proof the target is causal.

pathway_inference.label: Pathway / network inference
pathway_inference.description: The target sits in a pathway that is itself linked to the disease, without direct target-disease evidence.
pathway_inference.citation: Pathway and systems-biology inference is integrated as evidence by Open Targets; it is also the mechanism by which literature-based discovery proposes new links (Swanson's ABC model).

acquisition.name: Pathway-level functional readout
acquisition.description: Confirm the target actually moves the pathway node the inference depends on, in a human system.

literature_cooccurrence.label: Literature co-occurrence
literature_cooccurrence.description: Target and disease are discussed together in the literature.
literature_cooccurrence.citation: Literature evidence is an Open Targets datatype, but co-mention is dominated by how well studied a gene already is, so it systematically re-ranks the crowded targets to the top.

acquisition.name: Systematic literature triage
acquisition.description: Included so the planner can price it and then, correctly, almost never recommend it.

clinical_precedent.label: Clinical precedent in a related indication
clinical_precedent.description: A modulator of this target has shown efficacy in humans in a different but mechanistically related disease.
clinical_precedent.citation: Precedent transfers when the mechanism is shared and the tissue context matches; it does not transfer across tissue context (IL-17 blockade is effective in psoriasis and worsened Crohn's disease).

acquisition.name: Proof-of-mechanism study in the new indication
acquisition.description: A small biomarker-driven human study with the existing molecule. Expensive but nearly decisive.

direction_conflict.rationale: When atoms disagree about whether to inhibit or activate, the class is heavily discounted and the hypothesis is flagged as not-yet-actionable. A direction conflict is not a small uncertainty -- it means half the evidence argues for the opposite molecule.

context_mismatch.rationale: Evidence generated in a tissue that is not where the pathology lives is downweighted. Named after the IL-17 case: strong, replicated, correct biology in skin, and harm in gut.

refuting_atom.rationale: Atoms marked refutes:true contribute a negative log-LR of equal magnitude. Failed replications and negative clinical readouts have to be able to move the score down, or the ledger only ever accumulates.

tractability_weights.note: Weights reflect development risk per modality, not chemistry difficulty. Under 5% of the human proteome has been successfully drugged, and Target 2035 exists precisely because most proteins still lack a chemical or biological probe -- so tractability is reported as a separate coordinate, never folded into the probability that the biology is right.

novelty.rationale: Novelty is 1 - (co-mentions / saturation), floored at 0. A target-disease pair with 40+ co-mentions is not a new idea; the value of the engine there is arbitration, not discovery.
